long_biography.plain_text:
Boyd learned the trade in Pasadena, Texas, where his father, Richard, developed Ford's Pest Control into a formulation and distribution operation. Mark helped the family enterprise expand before building CSI around the manufacture and sale of insecticides, pesticides and related formulations. Its reach eventually extended from professional users to home-and-garden and production-animal customers.

Makhteshim Agan bought 45 per cent of the company in 2004 and later increased its interest under the ADAMA name. Boyd guided the enterprise as it absorbed Quali-Pro and acquired Bonide, broadening its product channels. After Boyd stepped down, Trey Kendrick assumed the chief executive role and CSI joined ADAMA's consolidated professional-solutions unit.

uncertainties.detail: The authoritative owner export links Mark Boyd, Control Solutions, Cherry Bomb and Lucky Lady. Current company, court, state and LinkedIn evidence independently resolves the exact specialty-chemicals founder, while public yacht pages confirm both matching vessels. Those public yacht pages do not name the owner, so the person-to-vessel link remains source-record based and identity confidence is capped at 92. Vessel facts are excluded from biographies, classifications and tags.

Public accounts describe Control Solutions as created in 1985, founded by Boyd in the 1990s or founded in 1998; the dossier therefore avoids an exact founding year. A primary filing establishes Makhteshim Agan's 45% acquisition in 2004, and a later filing reports ADAMA's 67.1% holding. Recent company material confirms CSI remains part of ADAMA, now within Syngenta Group, but Boyd's exact post-retirement percentage is not public. No personal transaction proceeds are inferred.

Boyd retired as Control Solutions president on 1 September 2025 and provided advisory support during the transition; current 2026 company material identifies Trey Kendrick as president and chief executive. No reliable source establishes a different principal post-retirement business or ranks Boyd's private holdings. Manufacturing is therefore retained under the explicit origin-sector fallback rule rather than presented as a continuing executive role.

Boyd is directly identified as Control Solutions' founder, but he entered the sector through the material operating experience, network and industry platform created by his father Richard. Control Solutions remained a distinct family-owned business after the older Ford's operation was sold, and no source says Mark inherited the principal CSI stake. Self-made — advantaged start is therefore more precise than Inherited, family transfer or an independent-start classification.

Control Solutions' official retirement post tags the proposed LinkedIn account, whose company, Seabrook location and education chronology independently match. A second sparse same-name LinkedIn account also associates with Control Solutions, but lacks the official cross-link and is excluded. Instagram, Personal Website, Facebook, Twitter/X, YouTube and TikTok searches produced no other personal account meeting the authentication threshold.

The authoritative 16 June 1958 birth date is preserved but not re-proposed. Public sources support male gender through consistent honorifics and pronouns. No reliable source established a middle name, birthplace, birth country or secondary nationality, so those fields remain blank.

Chemicals is the sole active assignment because pesticide and insecticide formulation is Boyd's defining wealth-creation and operating activity. The catalogue contains no active narrower pesticide or agrochemical owner tag, and Petrochemicals would be semantically wrong. No taxonomy candidate was created.
